one_liner: Twenty is an open-source CRM with APIs suitable for agent tools.

auth.notes: OAuth is documented for external apps acting on behalf of users; API keys are documented for internal scripts and automation.

access.notes: The free route is self-hosting. Twenty Cloud offers a time-limited trial.

api.notes: The public API guide is readable, but the interactive, workspace-specific reference requires a workspace and API key.

mcp.notes: Twenty says every Cloud workspace has a native MCP server.

verdict.rationale: Self-hosting the open-source core is free, and developers can create an API key. Documented REST and GraphQL APIs support CRUD on core and custom objects; OAuth is documented for apps acting on behalf of users.

evidence.quote: Build apps in TypeScript, connect your tools through APIs, and host Twenty yourself.

problems: The public API guide is readable, but the interactive reference is workspace-specific and available only after creating a key.
The pricing page describes a “30-day trial,” while the quickstart distinguishes a 30-day trial with a card from a 7-day trial without one; neither changes the free self-hosted route.
name: Twenty

verification.note: The quotes document OAuth for apps acting on behalf of users and API keys for internal scripts and automation.
Free self-hosting, a locally running API, and instructions to create an API key support a self-serve free path. The Cloud trial is also evidenced.
The public guide documents REST and GraphQL and CRUD on core and custom objects. It also confirms that workspace-specific documentation requires an API key.
Twenty's pricing page says every Cloud workspace ships with a native MCP server.
A Composio toolkit page for Twenty lists its MCP server.
The evidenced free self-hosted path to API credentials and documented, useful REST and GraphQL APIs support buildable_now with no main blocker.
